questions.q: Which document defines the seven tenets of Zero Trust Architecture covered in this lesson?
options: A vendor whitepaper from a ZTNA/SASE product vendor
NIST Special Publication 800-207, Zero Trust Architecture
The CIS Critical Security Controls
ISO/IEC 27001
questions.explain: NIST SP 800-207 is the real source document behind the industry's use of "Zero Trust," and Section 2.1 defines the seven tenets.

questions.q: Tenet 3 states that access to individual enterprise resources is granted on what basis?
options: Per-device, for the lifetime of that device
Per-user, for as long as their account is active
Per-session
Per-department, based on org chart membership
questions.explain: Access is granted per-session, not carried forward automatically — the architectural justification for short-lived tokens over long-lived "logged in all day" sessions.

questions.q: Which tenet justifies evaluating identity, device compliance, location, and risk signal together for every access decision, rather than just checking a password?
options: Tenet 1 — all data sources and computing services are considered resources
Tenet 2 — all communication is secured regardless of network location
Tenet 7 — the enterprise collects as much telemetry as possible to improve posture
Tenet 4 — access is determined by dynamic policy including identity, application, and asset state
questions.explain: Tenet 4 is the basis for Conditional Access-style policy: identity plus device plus context plus risk, evaluated together, every time — not a one-time password check.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does NIST deliberately avoid naming specific products in the seven tenets?
options: Because the tenets are architectural requirements that get satisfied with whatever combination of existing identity, policy, and monitoring controls a given enterprise already has
Because NIST does not endorse any security vendor by policy
Because product-based requirements would expire too quickly as vendors rebrand
Because the tenets only apply to government agencies, not private enterprises
questions.explain: The tenets describe what an architecture must satisfy, not what to buy — built from existing identity providers, cloud-native policy engines, EDR/XDR telemetry, and enforcement points.

questions.q: Tenet 5 — monitoring and measuring the integrity and security posture of all owned and associated assets — maps most directly to which practice you already know?
options: A one-time device compliance check performed during onboarding only
Continuous device posture checks, such as Intune compliance policies or AWS Systems Manager inventory
Annual penetration testing of production systems
Rotating a service account's password every 90 days
questions.explain: Tenet 5 requires continuous, ongoing posture verification — no device gets a permanent pass from a single past compliance check.
